sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Dougherty County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Dougherty County puts collection and valuation under one roof. The Tax Department answers to an appointed tax director, and no elected tax commissioner sits above it. Returns arrive there, and the office collects ad valorem tax on behalf of the county government, Albany city government, the school system and the state.

Its bills reach real estate, cars, business equipment, mobile homes and timber. The Board of Assessors operates inside the department and assigns each parcel its value. A parcel search runs through qPublic, and the county news page links a short video that walks through it.

  • Value, notice of assessment or appeal: Board of Assessors, 229-431-2130 or DocoAssessor@dougherty.ga.us.
  • County millage rate: voted on by the county commissioners.
  • School millage rate: voted on separately by the school board.
  • Paying a bill, bill dates and a payoff number for a closing: the Tax Department.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 revaluation change for Dougherty County owners?
sections.html:
Albany-area owners opened 2026 notices that came out of the county's first full revaluation in over a decade, and plenty of values moved sharply. A county release from August 31, 2026 repeats one point: the notice is an assessment and carries no payment due. It shows market value, homestead information and appeal steps. Taxes follow once appeals close and the digest and rates are final.

Commissioners explained at that meeting that valuation belongs to the assessors, while the commission handles the county budget and its own rate. They added that a bigger value need not mean a proportionally bigger county bill.

House Bill 581 adds a second layer. It limits annual growth in the taxable value of qualifying homesteads for each participating taxing authority, and counties, cities and school districts each had a choice to opt out. The local school board did opt out after public hearings, and the school system says existing homestead exemptions stay in place. A May 2026 state revenue briefing says SB 33, the HOME Act of 2026, ends the opt-out. The statewide floating exemption then applies from January 1, 2027, with 2026 values as the starting baseline. Ask the Tax Department what that means for your school bill.

The county says it will keep posting explanations of assessments, appeals, homestead exemptions and the millage-setting process on its website and social media pages.

sections.h2: How does a Dougherty County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
The appeal is a written filing to the Board of Assessors, due 45 days after the notice's mailing date. For 2026 the county published a cutoff of 11:59 p.m. on October 5, 2026, which is now behind us. Each future notice has its own mailing date, and the clock starts there.

State guidance lets an appeal argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and it uses a single statewide form. You declare your preferred route on that form, and the route decides who hears the case.

  • The county Board of Equalization.
  • A hearing officer.
  • An arbitrator.

County leaders encouraged owners whose value doubled or tripled to appeal, and the assessors answer questions at 229-431-2130. Useful evidence includes a recent sale of a comparable Albany house, contractor estimates and photos of damage.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments apply in Dougherty County?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption goes to people who held title and lived in the house on January 1. The state now allows filing through the 45-day appeal window as well as the old April 1 deadline. The standard state version removes $2,000 from the 40 percent assessed value for county and school tax, and an age 65 version removes $4,000 from county tax where household income stays within $10,000 for the prior year, after the retirement income exclusions the state describes.

Rural land follows separate rules. The Board of Assessors lists three programs, each requiring an application between January 1 and April 1 and a $25 fee:

  • Preferential agricultural assessment: bona fide farmland is assessed at 30 percent of fair market value rather than 40 percent.
  • Conservation use assessment: qualifying farm, timber, sensitive and transitional residential land is valued by current use.
  • Forest Land Protection Act: an exemption for land used in good faith to produce trees, timber or wood fiber.

Eligible owners are individuals, family farm corporations, estates, trusts and non-profits. They commit to the use for 10 years, and a single owner may enroll no more than 2,000 acres statewide. Check with the Tax Department for any local exemptions Dougherty County adds beyond the state list.

sections.h2: What do the Dougherty County numbers look like?
sections.html:
Dougherty County has lost residents since 2010, and renters now outnumber owners. Georgia's legislature created the county from Baker County in 1853. The county lists 326 square miles of land, quail plantations, Flint River recreation and cypress swamps among its draws. Albany State University and Albany Technical College supply higher education, while the Albany Civil Rights Institute and the Flint RiverQuarium bring in visitors.

sections.h2: What happens to the property tax bill when you sell a Dougherty County house?
sections.html:
Deed and lien searches run through the Clerk of Superior Court. Its real estate records can be searched online, and the office sits in the Judicial Building at 225 Pine Avenue, Suite 126, open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday at 229-431-2198. Pull the record on your own parcel before you list so a forgotten lien does not surprise anyone at closing.

Georgia assigns a year's tax to whoever held the property on January 1 and refunds nothing for a partial year. A seller who closes in March still faces a bill covering twelve months, so the purchase contract and settlement statement decide how the cost is divided. State guidance describes a typical 60-day payment window ending December 20, but the Tax Department supplies Dougherty County's actual dates.

Before you list, gather three things:

  • Your parcel number from qPublic and a copy of the 2026 notice.
  • A written balance from the Tax Department that shows any older unpaid years.
  • Your homestead status, which follows the January 1 owner and resident.

Albany houses with deferred repairs, tenants or an open estate sometimes sell as-is for cash, with the tax balance paid out of the proceeds. Liens are filed with the clerk, so confirm the balance and any recorded lien before you sign.

faqs.q: Does a Dougherty County assessment notice ask me to pay?
faqs.a: No. It reports market value, homestead details and appeal steps. Tax is calculated later, once appeals end, the digest is final and the county, city and school rates are adopted.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Dougherty appeal window still open?
faqs.a: No. Appeals on the 2026 notices closed at 11:59 p.m. on October 5, 2026. Later notices will show their own mailing dates and a fresh 45 days.

faqs.q: Which board votes on the millage rate in Dougherty County?
faqs.a: The commissioners vote on the county rate and the school board votes on the school rate. Assessors only determine value. The county rate comes after appeals end and the digest is complete.

faqs.q: Is the Dougherty school system in the HB 581 exemption?
faqs.a: It opted out after public hearings and says existing homestead exemptions remain. A May 2026 state briefing says SB 33 removes that option from January 1, 2027, so ask the Tax Department how it will reach your bill.

faqs.q: Do I still owe the full year's bill after selling in Albany?
faqs.a: Yes, on paper. Georgia holds the January 1 owner responsible and gives no partial-year refund. The settlement statement usually splits the cost with the buyer, so get the balance from the Tax Department first.
